transcriptClaims.claim:
**Yeah, I like it. This is substantially more than chair shuffling.** I read the full design and integration audit, then followed the current runtime, resolver, dispatch, capability fold, shared stream/result code, and representative tests.

The useful changes are concrete:

- **The package boundary does real work.** It depends on contracts and kit, receives persistence through ports, and exports one entry point. That makes inference independently exercisable without importing the server’s database or composition machinery. [package.json](/home/inktomi/inktomi-stack/development/orbweaver/packages/inference/package.json:10)
- **Providers and transports are finally different concepts.** Another compatible endpoint can be a provider row with features instead of another backend carrying slightly different history, retry, and parsing code. That reduces the number of places future fixes must land.
- **Selection has one executable home.** The binding fold, capability synthesis, and task dispatch are separate, understandable steps. Role clients resolve again at call time, so changing a binding affects the next call. [role-clients.ts](/home/inktomi/inktomi-stack/development/orbweaver/packages/inference/src/roles/role-clients.ts:105)
- **Normalization now preserves meaningful distinctions.** Requested versus applied settings, measured versus estimated cost, raw versus normalized termination, and replayable reasoning are actual behavioral improvements. The shared reducer’s handling of SDK-synthesized finishes is exactly the sort of defect one common implementation can prevent across transports. [stream.ts](/home/inktomi/inktomi-stack/development/orbweaver/packages/inference/src/backends/v4/stream.ts:234)

The conformance suite is particularly valuable: it tests whether different backends honor the same behavior, and makes missing drivers fail instead of quietly skipping coverage. That gives the abstraction teeth beyond matching method names.

**One concrete seam still looks unfinished:** background permission doesn’t appear enforced on the role-client execution path. Resolution emits a warning when `allowBackground` is false; `live()` takes only `resolved`, discarding that warning, and proceeds to the executor. Availability refuses it, but these calls don’t pass through availability. So switching background work off after binding appears insufficient to stop subsequent role-client calls. I traced this in source; I haven’t run a reproduction. [resolver](/home/inktomi/inktomi-stack/development/orbweaver/packages/inference/src/resolve/resolve-task.ts:281), [caller](/home/inktomi/inktomi-stack/development/orbweaver/packages/inference/src/roles/role-clients.ts:113)

My other criticism is the **documentation’s accumulated history**: the design mixes original requirements, superseded decisions, and later corrections. The code is considerably easier to understand than the document now. Once the remaining work settles, a concise account of the implemented architecture would help future readers avoid rebuilding something you deliberately removed.
